options.markdown:
Engagement Overview


Metrics about your users and the charts, detectors, dashboards, dashboard groups, and teams that they have created in SignalFx.
Metric: sf.org.num.orguser Total number of members and admins associated with an organization; includes invited users who have not yet logged in.
Metric: sf.org.num.team Number of teams in the organization.
Metric: sf.org.num.chart Total number of charts; includes any charts created using the SignalFx API but not associated with a dashboard.
Metric: sf.org.num.page Total number of dashboard groups; includes user, custom, and built-in dashboard groups.
Metric: sf.org.num.dashboard Total number of dashboards; includes all user, custom, and built-in dashboards.
Metric: sf.org.num.alertmuting Total number of alert muting rules; includes rules currently in effect and rules not currently in effect (e.g. scheduled muting rules).
Metric: sf.org.num.detector Total number of detectors; includes detectors that are muted.

sf.org.limit.hosts is maximum number of hosts that can send data to your organization. The limit is higher than your contractual limit to allow for burst and overage usage. If you exceed this limit, Infrastructure Monitoring drops data points from new hosts but keeps accepting data points for existing hosts. To monitor your usage against the limit, use the metric sf.org.numResourcesMonitored and filter for the dimension resourceType:hosts. This organization's host subscription entitlement is sf.org.subscription.hosts. This chart may be blank because some subscription types do not rely on a host entitlement.

By default, we offer each organization with a host subscription up to 500k bundle metrics. sf.org.numBundledMetrics represents the total number of bundled metrics being used in this organization. Hitting the bundle metrics limit results in no additional bundled metrics being created. Please see [documentation](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/admin/imm-billing-usage/monitor-imm-billing-usage.html) for more information about bundled metrics.

Infrastructure Monitoring Entitlements

Usage Notes:
The charts and data shown on this dashboard and for troubleshooting purposes only. For accounting purposes, please see your organization's Billing and Usage page and report. Please see Documentation for Splunk Infrastructure Monitoring Billing and Usage for more information.
Not all of entitlements shown on this page are applicable to all organizations; they can be blank.

sf.org.limit.customMetricTimeSeries is maximum number of active custom MTS, within a moving window of the previous 60 minutes, that can send data to your organization. If you exceed this limit, Infrastructure Monitoring drops data points for the custom MTS that exceeded the limit, but it continues to accept data points for custom MTS that already existed. you’ve defined, use the metric sf.org.numCustomMetrics. The number of custom MTS that can be monitored according to your subscription entitlement sf.org.subscription.customMetrics. To learn more about custom MTS, see [Splunk Observability Documentation](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/admin/imm-billing-usage/monitor-imm-billing-usage.html#about-custom-high-res). This chart may be blank because some subscription types do not rely on a host or custom metric entitlement.

sf.org.limit.containers is the maximum number of containers that can send data to your organization. This limit is higher than your contractual limit to allow for burst and overage usage. If you exceed this limit, Infrastructure Monitoring drops data points from new containers but keeps accepting data points for existing containers. To monitor your usage against the limit, use the metric sf.org.numResourcesMonitored and filter for the dimension resourceType:containers. This organization's container subscription entitlement is sf.org.subscription.container. This chart may be blank because some subscription types do not rely on a host entitlement.

Key Application Performance Monitoring Throttling Metrics


These charts highlight metrics that track throttling and limiting in your organization. It can be used to identify if there is currently any throttling taking place. If any of the charts on this dashboard indicate that there is throttling, use the information in the APM Entitlements dashboard to help identify where you can reduce usage.
These charts are for troubleshooting purposes only. For accounting purposes, please see your organization's Subscription Usage page and report.

chart.name: Span Drop Due to Ingest Limits

options.markdown: sf.org.apm.numSpansDroppedThrottle is the number of spans that APM was unable to process or has dropped because you significantly exceeded your trace volume or ingest limit. sf.org.apm.numSpansDroppedThrottleByToken is the number of spans by token that APM was unable to process or has dropped because you significantly exceeded your trace volume or ingest imit.
sf.org.apm.numSpanBytesReceived represents the trace volume. This organization's Trace Volume subscription entitlement is sf.org.apm.subscription.numSpanBytesReceived.

sf.org.apm.numSpansDroppedBlocked is the number of spans that APM was unable to process or has dropped because they are blockedTraceId or tooManySpansInTrace. Different reasons are explained here: blockedTraceID: Trace has over 1M spans tooManySpansInTrace: Trace submitted over 100k spans to a single ingest instance

Application Performance Monitoring Entitlements

Usage Notes:
The charts and data shown on this dashboard are for troubleshooting purposes only. Please be mindful that there will be a delay in the data shown on the Subscription Usage page when compared to the data shown on this dashboard. For accounting purposes, please see your organization's Subscription Usage page and report. Please see Documentation for Splunk Application Performance Monitoring Subscription Usage for more information.
Not all of the entitlements shown on this page are applicable to all organizations; they can be blank.

sf.org.apm.numContainers represents the number of containers that are actively sending data to Splunk APM at 1 minute resolution. This organization's container subscription entitlement is sf.org.apm.subscription.containers. This chart may be blank because some subscription types do not rely on a host entitlement.

sf.org.apm.numTracesReceived represents the number of traces analyzed per minute. This organization's TAPM subscription entitlement is sf.org.apm.subscription.traces. This chart may be blank because some subscription types do not rely on a TAPM entitlement.

Infrastructure Monitoring System Limits


These charts identify metrics that track usage of system limits in your organization. If a metric is reported for the limit, it is included in the chart as well.

For more information about system limits in the Splunk Observability Cloud, please see Documentation for System Limits

sf.org.limit.customMetricTimeSeries is maximum number of active custom MTS, within a moving window of the previous 60 minutes, that can send data to your organization. If you exceed this limit, Infrastructure Monitoring drops data points for the custom MTS that exceeded the limit, but it continues to accept data points for custom MTS that already existed. you’ve defined, use the metric sf.org.numCustomMetrics. The number of custom MTS that can be monitored according to your subscription entitlement sf.org.subscription.customMetrics. To learn more about custom MTS, see [Splunk Observability Documentation](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/admin/imm-billing-usage/monitor-imm-billing-usage.html#about-custom-high-res).

sf.org.limit.metricTimeSeriesCreatedPerMinute is the maximum rate at which you can create new MTS in your organization, measured in MTS per minute. If you exceed this rate, Infrastructure Monitoring stops accepting data points for new MTS, but continues to accept data points for existing MTS. To monitor the number of metrics you’ve created overall, use the metric sf.org.numMetricTimeSeriesCreated.
sf.org.numDatapointsReceived is the total number of datapoints received in this organization.

options.markdown: sf.org.num.detector is the number of detectors that exist in this organization and sf.org.limit.detector is the total number of detectors you can create. Attempting to create new detectors will fail when this limit is hit. Note: Base AutoDetect detectors and token limit detectors do not count towards this limit and sf.org.num.detector has filters applied (purpose:CUSTOM) so that it accurately represents the detectors that count towards the limit.

sf.org.limit.containers is the maximum number of containers that can send data to your organization. This limit is higher than your contractual limit to allow for burst and overage usage. If you exceed this limit, Infrastructure Monitoring drops data points from new containers but keeps accepting data points for existing containers. To monitor your usage against the limit, use the metric sf.org.numResourcesMonitored and filter for the dimension resourceType:containers. This organization's container subscription entitlement is sf.org.subscription.container.

sf.org.numRestCalls is the number of API calls made per minute in this organization.
The limit is 100,000 API calls per minute for most organizations.

sf.org.numCustomMetrics is the number of MTS that have received a datapoint in the past hour and sf.org.limit.customMetricTimeSeries is the limit. Hitting this limit results in no new MTS being created until active MTS go inactive by not receiving a datapoint for an hour.

sf.org.limit.hosts is maximum number of hosts that can send data to your organization. The limit is higher than your contractual limit to allow for burst and overage usage. If you exceed this limit, Infrastructure Monitoring drops data points from new hosts but keeps accepting data points for existing hosts. To monitor your usage against the limit, use the metric sf.org.numResourcesMonitored and filter for the dimension resourceType:hosts. This organization's host subscription entitlement is sf.org.subscription.hosts. Some subscription types do not contain hosts so this chart may be blank.

sf.org.numInactiveTimeSeries identifies the total number of Inactive MTS being used in this organization. The limit depends on your contract. Hitting this limit results in Inactive MTS being deleted starting with the oldest MTS.

options.markdown:
Token Limits are an enterprise feature in Splunk Observability that allows you do place a limit on how much a particular token can ingest. Please see [documentation](https://docs.splunk.com/Observability/admin/authentication-tokens/manage-usage.html#cost-related-token-limits) for more information about token limits.

This chart shows the percentage of datapoints for each token that are being dropped because of throttling. If many tokens show up in this chart with  >0% of datapoints dropped, it is probably because of an organization-wide throttle. If only a couple tokens are being throttled, as shown in the chart, it is probably related to a token limit throttle. Clicking in the chart will show you a table with the token names that are being throttled. A banner should also appear at the top of the page if a token has gone above its token limit.
sf.org.numLimitedEventTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the number of ETS that Splunk Observability was unable to create because you exceeded the maximum ETS allowed.

sf.org.numLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the total number of MTS that cannot be created in Splunk Observability because this organization has reached the limit for active MTS or a subscription-related limit. Subscription-related limits include hosts, containers, custom metrics, bundled metrics, functions, high resolution metrics, APM metrics, or APM bundled metrics. sf.org.numLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCallsByCategoryType is the number of MTS that cannot be created because of subscription-related limits.

sf.org.numPropertyLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the number of metric time series (MTS) Infrastructure Monitoring was unable to create because you reached your maximum number of unique dimension names.

sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedExceededQuota is the total number of new data points you sent to Infrastructure Monitoring but that Infrastructure Monitoring didn't accept, because your organization exceeded its subscription limit.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedThrottle is the total number of data points that Splunk Observability did not accept because your organization significantly exceeded its DPM limit. Hitting this limit means that new datapoints are not accepted for existing and new MTS.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedBatchSize is the number of data points dropped because a single request contained more than 100,000 data points.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedInTimeout is the number of data points Observability Cloud didn't attempt to create because your account was throttled or limited in the previous few seconds and creation was unlikely to succeed.
sf.org.numDatapointsDroppedInvalid is the number of data points dropped because they didn't follow documented guidelines for data points. For example, the metric name was too long, the metric name included unsupported characters, or the data point contained no values.

chart.name: Token Throttling
chart.programText:
A = data('sf.org.numDatapointsDropped*ByToken', rollup='sum', extrapolation='zero').sum(by=['tokenId', 'tokenName']).publish(label='A', enable=False)
H = data('sf.org.numDatapointsReceivedByToken', rollup='sum', extrapolation='zero').sum(by=['tokenId', 'tokenName']).publish(label='H', enable=False)
I = (A/(A+H)*100).publish(label='I')
J = alerts(detector_name='Category Limit Alert Threshold*').publish(label='J')

options.markdown: sf.org.numThrottledMetricTimeSeriesCreateCalls is the number of metric time series (MTS) that Infrastructure Monitoring was unable to create because you significantly exceeded your per-minute or per-hour MTS creation limit.

sf.org.numLimitedMetricTimeSeriesCreateCallsByCategoryType is the number of MTS that cannot be created because of subscription-related limits, including hosts, containers, custom metrics, bundled metrics, functions, high resolution metrics, APM metrics, or APM bundled metrics. This chart breaks out each of these limits separately so that you can see which limit is preventing MTS from being created.
Note: Subscription limits shown depends on your plan so not all of these will be shown.

Key Infrastructure Monitoring Throttling Metrics


These charts highlight metrics that track throttling and limiting in your organization. It can be used to identify if there is currently any throttling taking place. If any of the charts on the this dashboard indicate that there is throttling, use the information in the System Limits and Entitlements dashboards to help identify where you can reduce usage.
These charts are for troubleshooting purposes only. For accounting purposes, please see your organization's Billing and Usage page and report.

For more information about system limits in the Splunk Infrastructure Monitoring, please see Documentation for System Limits
